content:
The image shows a very early seedling (cotyledon stage) emerging from moist soil, surrounded by crop residue. The seedling appears stunted and barely emerged, with no normal hypocotyl development visible. The soil is wet/dark.

Key observations:
- Very early seedling emergence failure or severe stunting at soil level
- Moist, wet soil conditions
- The seedling is either failing to emerge properly or has a collapsed/rotted hypocotyl
- No leaf disease symptoms visible (it's a seedling stage issue)
- Wet conditions strongly favor water mold pathogens

This presentation is consistent with **Pythium damping-off**: pre-emergence or post-emergence damping-off caused by Pythium spp., favored by cool, wet soils. The seedling is barely emerging with what appears to be a collapsed or blighted cotyledon/hypocotyl at the soil line — classic post-emergence damping-off. Rhizoctonia can also cause damping-off, but Rhizoctonia tends to cause a more distinct reddish-brown lesion on the hypocotyl and occurs more in warmer conditions. The very wet soil and near-total collapse at emergence fits Pythium better.
